fixtures.city_amends_note: A New York city can set a construction standard stricter than the Uniform Code only with the State Fire Prevention and Building Code Council's approval (Executive Law section 379, state pack). The Council's page lists the approved standards: one Uniform Code item (Village of Saltaire, sprinklers in single-family houses) and two energy code filings (Town of Ithaca, City of New York). Rochester is not on it, so the state's toilet-count table and rules apply unchanged and the state pack's worked examples stand. The list excludes petitions still pending.

permit.exempt_list_quote: [State rule every city's code enforcement program must follow, 19 NYCRR 1203.3(a)(1), read on Cornell LII] Each authority having jurisdiction shall include in its code enforcement program provisions requiring building permits to be required for work that must conform to either or both of the Codes. Where expressly set forth in their code enforcement program, an authority having jurisdiction may exempt from the requirement for a building permit any one or more of the categories of work listed in section 1203.3 (a)(1)(i) through (viii). An exemption from the requirement to obtain a building permit shall not be deemed an authorization for work to be performed in violation of either or both of the Codes. The following categories of work may be exempted from the requirement for a building permit: [...] (iv) installation of partitions or movable cases less than 5'-9" in height; (v) painting, wallpapering, tiling, carpeting, or other similar finish work; (vi) installation of listed portable electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, or cooling equipment or appliances; (vii) replacement of any equipment provided the replacement does not alter the equipment's listing or render it inconsistent with the equipment's original specifications; and (viii) repairs, provided that the work does not have an impact on fire and life safety, such as: (a) any part of the structural system; (b) the required means of egress; or (c) the fire protection system or the removal from service of any part of the fire protection system for any period of time.
permit.city_list_note: Rochester's own list is Municipal Code section 39-207 (When building permit required), subsection B. It was NOT read. ecode360.com (the city's code host) and cityofrochester.gov both answer automated requests with a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403), so the section text was not opened; what is recorded comes from web-search excerpts of those pages and is not a verbatim reading. Search excerpts report: a building permit is required 'for any work which must conform to the Building Code and/or the Energy Code'; subsection B begins 'No building permit shall be required for work in any of the following categories' and includes the 'installation of partitions or movable cases' under five feet nine inches tall and repairs that do not touch load-bearing walls or structural members, required egress, building systems or fire protection systems; section 39-202 says repair to existing structures does not require a building permit except as specifically provided. Search excerpts of the city's Building Permits page and its handout 'General Guidelines for Work "Not" Requiring a Building Permit' report: no permit for minor repairs, for 'removal, replacement, or covering of interior finishes (carpet, vinyl flooring, wallpaper, paint, etc.)' or for 'casework or cabinet replacements that do not change the layout of the space'; changing layouts, adding walls, altering systems or affecting structure needs an application; the list 'is not intended to be all-inclusive'. No excerpt mentions toilet partitions.
permit.partitions_named_note: Neither the state list nor any excerpt of the city's list names toilet partitions. Both name 'partitions or movable cases' under 5 ft 9 in; whether that covers floor-anchored or overhead-braced toilet partitions (pilasters are usually taller than 5 ft 9 in) is for the Permit Office to say.

restrooms_city.rule: Rochester Ordinance No. 2025-283 (passed by City Council August 26, 2025, deemed adopted August 27, 2025, effective immediately) amended Municipal Code Chapter 63, Human Rights. Section 63-3(A) now makes it unlawful, due to discrimination, for the owner, lessee, proprietor, manager, superintendent, agent or employee of a place of public accommodation, resort or amusement to deny access to a public bathroom designated for the gender most consistent with the patron's gender identity or expression, to restrict the use of a single-use bathroom to a particular gender, or to require transgender individuals to use only a single-use bathroom. Section 63-9 still allows separate bathrooms for males and females, provided their use is not unlawfully restricted. The ordinance sets no sign wording and no building requirement, and says nothing on shared all-gender rooms.
restrooms_city.quote: §63-3 A. It shall be unlawful, due to discrimination, for any person, being the owner, lessee, proprietor, manager, superintendent, agent or employee of any place of public accommodation, resort or amusement, to directly or indirectly: (1) Deny access to a public bathroom, locker room, dressing room or bathing facility that is designated for a gender that is most consistent or most closely aligned with the patron's gender identity or expression; (2) Restrict the use of a single-use bathroom to a particular gender, or require transgender individuals to use only a single-use bathroom; [...] §63-9 [...] It shall not be a violation of this chapter for any person to: (1) Maintain separate bathrooms, locker rooms and bathing facilities for males and females, provided that their use is not unlawfully restricted in violation of §63-3; [...] Section 3. This ordinance shall take effect immediately.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Rochester job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the New York rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Rochester offices, university buildings, hospitals and manufacturing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** New York's statewide building rules, which Rochester enforces, set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Rochester requires a building permit for work that has to meet the building rules. New York lets each city exempt some small jobs, such as painting, tiling and similar finish work, and partitions or movable cases under 5 feet 9 inches tall. That list doesn't name toilet partitions, and Rochester keeps its own list, so ask the City of Rochester Permit Office (585-428-6526) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** New York law requires every one-person restroom in a public place, school or state building to be marked gender neutral, with the sign on or near the door. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own stall with a door and each urinal is screened; it is not signed by sex, and its toilets are counted from the building's whole capacity. A Rochester ordinance adds that a business or other place open to the public may not limit a one-person bathroom to one gender, require transgender people to use only a one-person bathroom, or refuse a patron the public bathroom designated for the gender that matches their gender identity. Separate men's and women's rooms remain allowed.
page.confirm_office: the City of Rochester Permit Office
page.stalls_intro: Rochester uses New York's statewide rules, which count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs its own stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they can replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. A restaurant's count includes seasonal outdoor seating. The state lists no stricter local standard for Rochester.
page.install_rule: Rochester's city code sets no general contractor license. A permit application comes from the owner, an agent, an architect, an engineer or the contractor, who must make sure all required contractors are licensed. New York State does not license commercial installers like this. Confirm what your project needs with the City of Rochester Permit Office. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Rochester has no general contractor license, and New York State doesn't license this work.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on public work, such as school, city, county and state projects, New York law requires at least the prevailing wage for the trade, with no minimum contract size; the state Department of Labor publishes the rates by county each July. For a carpenter on building work in Monroe County that is $37.03 an hour plus $25.07 in benefits, on the schedule for July 2026 through June 2027.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8% in Rochester: 4% state and 4% Monroe County. The city adds no sales tax of its own.
page.buyers_extra: - **Universities, hospitals and manufacturing plants:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE where stalls take hard use.
